body:
I've found a solution to the same problem in Godot 4 in [this Reddit post ("Child nodes duplicating when loading a packed scene").](https://www.reddit.com/r/godot/comments/1au46aw/child_nodes_duplicating_when_loading_a_packed/) I've copied the details below. 

A quick search for `scene_file_path` in the 3.6 docs doesn't return anything, so presumably this solution is not valid for 3.x, but maybe it will help someone solve it.

Copy of the Reddit post:

### Child nodes duplicating when loading a packed scene

I'm saving my game by looping through the scene tree, setting every node's Owner as the game instance node, and packing the game instance into a compressed packed scene.

This approach works except that any scene instances under the game instance will make duplicates of their children when you load the packed scene. Like the player now has two animation players and cameras, torches have two omnilights so on.

If the duplicates are deleted everything works as intended. It seems that both the scene's original nodes and the saved version of those nodes is being added when the pack scene is instanced. If I look at the packed scene in the editor, the duplicates aren't there. They only appear when I instance the scene in game

### Answer

 I realize that it's been quite a long time since you asked this question, but I was struggling with literally the same thing. The issue is that if you don't clear a node's "scene_file_path" value before you pack it, it will pack as a sub-packed-scene, and then when you load it in the editor, it double-loads. In summary the fix is this:
when you loop through your node's children, to set their owner, also add this:
`child_node.scene_file_path = ""`
that'll fix it.
